I’ve been farming these plots in Quzhou for more than twenty years, and wheat-maize double cropping is what I know best. Last year my wheat hit about 1,000 jin per mu and the maize did even better, so I’m not about to change a winning system. I’ll plant improved wheat—probably Jimai 22—on all 8 mu in early October, after rotary tilling to break up the stubble. For fertilizer I’ll put down 100 kg of compound (18-22-5) as basal, then topdress with 50 kg of urea per mu when the wheat greens up in spring. I’ll irrigate four times: winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Weeds and insects are always a problem, so I’ll spray herbicide once and do two more passes for insects and fungus. Right after wheat harvest in mid-June I’ll no-till plant hybrid maize—Denghai 605—on the same 8 mu because there’s barely a week between crops. I’ll spread 80 kg of compound (28-6-6) at sowing and irrigate twice if the summer turns dry. Maize gets herbicide once and insecticide twice. I thought about cotton, but the labor is heavy and the price bounces around too much; wheat and maize have steady buyers and the government buys wheat at a floor price, so that’s safer for my family.
